sections: Enterprise Security and SOAR pricing models
claimChecks.evidence: Essentials and Premier remain distinct editions. The 30-day Essentials and 90-day Premier trial behavior remains documented. Public activity/workload/ingest descriptions do not establish customer price, feature entitlement or a deployment-specific commercial authorization.
claimChecks.qualification: Edition grouping, licensing, trials and public pricing models assessed separately from feature entitlement and customer contracts.

claimChecks.evidence: The 8.7.0/8.7.1/8.7.2 milestones and the November 4 ES 8.8 GA milestone remain distinct. Current 8.8 agent corrections were not applied retrospectively to 8.7 statements.
claimChecks.qualification: Release stage and historical entitlement boundaries remain version-specific.

sections: Cloud Connect scope and access prerequisites
claimChecks.evidence: The current regional tables retain different Essentials, Premier and Cloud Connect coverage and GCP/Azure qualifications. Cloud Connect administration does not establish a feature edition, rollout, regulated authorization or customer enablement.
claimChecks.qualification: Regional availability is not offering authorization; regulated gaps remain with CSP FedRAMP Watch.

sections: Workflow and feature availability by edition
claimChecks.evidence: The current SAIA 2.4.0 installer now documents a versioned Cloud Connect path. The ES 8.8 agent table now separates Triage from Controlled Availability Autonomous Response. Exact App for SOAR and Export rows remain functionality-tested matrices and do not infer pairing from independent release numbers.
claimChecks.qualification: Installation, feature stage, edition, exact pairing, region, entitlement, enablement and authorization remain separate.

claimChecks.evidence: SAIA 2.4.0 now supplies the documented Cloud Connect install path with Enterprise 10.4+, Cloud Connect 2.0+, paid-license, fresh-setup, network, certificate, permission, verified-email-domain and supported-commercial-region conditions. It does not establish ES feature entitlement, rollout or authorization.
claimChecks.qualification: Essentials Cloud and Premier Cloud/Cloud Connected scope remains edition-qualified.

claimChecks.evidence: Detection Builder remains Essentials and Premier. Cloud requires Platform 10.1+ and ES 8.6+; CMP requires Platform 10.4+, ES 8.8+, Cloud Connect 2.0+ and SAIA 2.4+. The 8.8 task guide says finding-based Detection Builder is turned off.
claimChecks.qualification: The released dependency path does not imply universal feature rollout, entitlement, region or authorization.

claimChecks.evidence: SOP remains Essentials and Premier on Cloud, dependent on Security AI Assistant and response-template view/edit permissions.
claimChecks.qualification: No CMP, first-availability, entitlement or authorization inference.

claimChecks.evidence: Threat Graph remains alpha for Premier 8.8, with representative enablement, at least one risk-based detection, approximately one million events and test mode.
claimChecks.qualification: ES 8.8 product GA does not promote this alpha feature or establish customer authorization.

sections: Separate Triage and Autonomous Response rows
claimChecks.evidence: Triage is now an explicit Premier Cloud/CMP component. Autonomous Response is separately Controlled Availability; its row says Cloud only while also listing a CMP prerequisite, so CMP availability remains conflicting. The Platform/ES minimum discrepancy, paired-SOAR requirement, first-10/~200-per-tenant limits, frontier-model condition and connector/asset permissions remain.
claimChecks.qualification: Exact SOAR pairing, region, entitlement, enablement and customer authorization remain separate.

claimChecks.evidence: The advisor decision now distinguishes the current Premier Triage component from Controlled Availability Autonomous Response and recognizes the versioned 2.4 Cloud Connect path while retaining the Cloud ES floor discrepancy and CMP availability conflict.
claimChecks.qualification: Registered exclusions for exact SOAR pairing, agent rollout, entitlement and authorization remain intact.
